topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement lecture and frames its complexity and clinical importance.

topics.label: Fundamentals and general principles of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the basic principles, naming rules, and the central molecular fulcrum governing the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the three recognition pathways that activate the complement cascade and establish a localized trigger threshold.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement executes its destructive and immune-recruiting effector functions.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activation on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how host cells utilize regulatory proteins to protect themselves from complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the diverse clinical presentations and disease phenotypes arising from deficiencies in different complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement and applications of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement destruction and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer delivers concluding remarks and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
